_doc: cm#185 schema bring-forward manifest. Cross-checked against each file's own in-file header directive (first non-blank lines: '-- handoff:dialect postgres' | '-- handoff:dialect sqlite' | '-- handoff:excluded <reason>') by scripts/lib/schema-classify.js. This file provides CLASSIFICATION + EXPECTED-OBJECTS metadata only -- it is never the source of enumeration. Enumeration always reads the filesystem (scripts/sql/*.sql, non-recursive) and cross-checks git-tracked status; any enumerated file absent from this manifest, or any manifest entry whose classification disagrees with the file's own header directive, is a loud classification error (persistent project_settings 'schema_apply_degraded' row + stderr), never a silent skip. schema_epoch is a monotonically-bumped integer bumped whenever the applicable-unit set or any unit's DDL changes in a way that must force a re-apply on already-current databases; it is embedded as the '<epoch>:<hash>' prefix of the stored project_settings.schema_fingerprint value (see _computeSchemaFingerprint in scripts/handoff.js).

expected_objects._note: The pgvector-gated assertions.embedding column, assertions_embedding_hnsw_idx, and the pg_trgm-gated assertions_trgm_text_idx are deliberately EXCLUDED from this expected-objects list. Both DO $$ blocks that create them are designed to degrade gracefully (EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS) when the extension is absent -- the file's own header states 'no extensions, no halfvec, no pgvector dependency'. Including them here would convert an intentional optional degrade into a permanent stuck-degraded state on every stock Postgres instance without pgvector/pg_trgm installed. See PR body for the full rationale (S-13 scope interpretation).

decisions-base.sql._note: The pgvector-gated decisions.embedding column and decisions_embedding_idx HNSW index are deliberately EXCLUDED from expected_objects -- same rationale as handoff-core-schema.sql's own _note: both are wrapped in DO $$ blocks with EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS so a pgvector-absent target degrades gracefully, and including them here would convert that intentional optional degrade into a permanent stuck-degraded state on any stock Postgres instance without pgvector. The decisions_audit trigger and log_guarded_change() function are also excluded from expected_objects: schemaObjectsExist() only probes tables/columns/indexes (see db-seam.js), it has no trigger/function probe, so there is nothing meaningful to add there -- their presence is instead proven by test/test-decisions-canon.js's live INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE + audit_log assertion (cm#224 S6).
